chapter: Raymond Scott, Kirby and postwar bands
title: Barnet's black-and-white band and the Apollo Theatre
summary: Barnet's integrated band was the first white band to play the Apollo, 21 times, with Trummy Young, Peanuts Holland, Clark Terry and Doc Severinsen in different editions.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well, he joined, just after I left Barnet, we heard him from Boston. You see, with Barnet's band -- which I hadn't touched on before because we skipped over so many things -- we played the Apollo Theatre 21 times. We were the first white band to play the Apollo Theatre, and of course, we always had a black and white band. Now after Benny Goodman ...
Oh, yes; that's the way Barnet wanted it. That's the way it was.
What was the percentage? What -- who were the blacks in the band? Trummy Young.
Well, we had so many bands and so many different musicians.
But Peanuts Holland was in there.
And you had Al Killian. Right?
That was during when I was at home; they were out on the coast then.
That was during the era -- and he had Clark Terry, but that was during the era that I had gone home in '45.
Uh huh. And Doc Severinson. They were in there.

Doc Severinson came back, and in '48 with a new band that we're just talking about. Doc Severinson was a young kid. Who else was in that band? Goodness ... Bunny Briggs was with us, played 'East Side, West Side, All Around The Town', which was another hit.
We went into Bop City with that band, which was the same place with another name.
